The most recently ADDED records of a business object, straight from the database. Use for "latest invoice added", "last 5 sale orders", "newest customers", "most recent POS orders". Returns a ready data table; write one short sentence highlighting the newest item.

Find records semantically similar to a natural-language query (vector cosine search over pgvector). Use when the user references a record by paraphrase ("the deal with Acme construction", "leads that look like the one I closed last week", "policies about overtime") rather than an exact identifier. The result is a pipe-CSV `id|name|score|hint1|hint2` — cite ids in your answer, do not invent fields. model: technical model name (e.g. 'crm.lead', 'res.partner', 'ai.chat.fact'); query: the search text. Only models that have been embedded return useful results — when count=0, fall back to other tools.

List the apps this user can open

List the apps and sections THIS user is actually allowed to open, read live from their menu access. Call it whenever the user asks what the system can do for them, what they have access to, or where to start ("what can I do here?", "ما الذي يمكنني فعله؟", "I'm new, help me"). Ground your answer only in what it returns — never mention an app that is absent from the result, because the user cannot open it.

Resolve "where do I do X?" into real menu entries this user can open, with the full path and the action behind it. Use for any how-do-I / where-is question ("where do I create a credit note?", "وين أسوي فاتورة مرتجع؟", "how do I add an employee?"). Each match carries an action_xmlid you can pass to open_action so the answer includes a working button. An empty result means the WORD did not match, which is not the same as no access: if you searched in a language other than English, search again with the English term before drawing any conclusion.
